SMTO-PRX-0019 — Your Proxmox sign-in ran out while making a change

GUID: 25a4fd68-194b-4bbe-a928-6ab92b356450
Slug: proxmox-session-expired
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • Proxmox rejected SMTO's saved sign-in while SMTO was sending a change. SMTO did not send the change a second time, so check whether it happened before asking again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to show the current status of the VM or item you were changing, without changing anything. This shows whether Proxmox carried out the change before the sign-in ran out.
  2. If the change didn't happen, ask for it again. The expired sign-in was cleared, so SMTO signs in again with the saved username and password.
  3. If you then see a sign-in error, open Parameter Store, select your Proxmox parameter, open the Value tab, select Reveal & edit value, update "password", and select Save. A password changed on Proxmox makes the saved one stop working.

What success looks like

  • The Agent completes the change and the VM's status shows the result you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Proxmox server. Don't type your password into the chat; keep it only in the Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Proxmox returned 401 to a write request on an existing Gateway session (http_session_expired); the Gateway cleared the session and did not replay the mutation.

What this means

  • The HTTP session layer explicitly reports http_session_expired and the Proxmox client preserves that classification. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • The HTTP session layer explicitly reports http_session_expired and the Proxmox client preserves that classification.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact session/profile scope and original write receipt before renewing credentials.

How to fix it

  • Read the target resource state to confirm whether the mutation applied, then reissue it if needed; the cleared session means the next request performs a fresh /api2/json/access/ticket login. If that login fails, correct the Proxmox Server parameter's credentials; never pass them in task text.
  • Reauthenticate or renew the intended session through the supported flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended session is renewed through supported controls and any earlier mutation is reconciled first.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
